The Craft

Old-school hands, Gulfton heart

Chuchu Barber Shop 9536 is a working neighbourhood barbershop on Richmond Avenue — not a chain, not a concept store. A chair, a razor, and the time to do the job properly.

Where we are

Richmond Ave, in the middle of it all

Suite A at 9536 Richmond Avenue puts the shop in the heart of Gulfton, where Houston's whole world passes the door — office workers from the Galleria side, families from Sharpstown and Alief, regulars who have sat in the same chair for years.

The shop covers the essentials and covers them properly: men's cuts, straight razor shaves, beard sculpts, line-ups and colour. Nothing on the board is there to fill space — if it is listed, it is done well and done daily.

That is how a 4.9-star rating from 65 Google reviews gets built: one chair, one client, one clean finish at a time.

The shave ritual

Why the razor still rules

Cartridges are fast. A straight razor is better. Here is the full ritual, the way it runs at Chuchu.

1

Steam & soften

A hot towel rests on the face for a full minute — pores open, whiskers soften, skin relaxes.

2

Lather up

Rich, warm lather worked in properly, lifting every hair away from the skin.

3

The blade

A fresh straight razor, short steady strokes — with the grain, then against it for the close finish.

4

Cold close

A cold towel and a steady hand on the edges. Skin calm, jawline sharp, out the door.
